summary: George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1861–1862). He held a post at University College London from around 1866 to 1892 and taught Caroline Rhys Davids.

George Cœdès studied at the EPHE and University of Berlin under Finot, Lévi, Foucher, and Pischel. A scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology, he directed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929) and the EFEO (1929–1947).

George D. Bond works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he became Professor of Religion around 1974.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard University (1903–1905). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George E. Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1976). He worked at Johns Hopkins (1975–1978) and Princeton (1978–1986), taking the chair in Indo-European studies at Zurich in 1986.

George Foot Moore, a religious studies scholar, earned a bachelor's at Yale (1870–1872) and studied at Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877). He taught at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and served as Frothingham Professor at Harvard (1904–1928).

George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He spent his career on the faculty at Harvard University from around 1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart earned a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1963–1971). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1974) and served as professor at UC Berkeley (~1974–2013), which he founded.

George Lakoff studied at MIT (~1958–1962) and Indiana University (~1962–1966). Active in linguistics and philosophy, he taught linguistics at Harvard (1965–1969), founded the Rockridge Institute (2003), and was professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins (doctorate ~1891–1897). An Indologist and linguist, he taught at Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and served as professor of Greek at Ohio State University (1914–1939).

George Quasha, active in religious studies and Tibetology, founded Barrytown/Station Hill Press. He has taught at Stony Brook University (~1968–1971), Bard College (~1974), The New School, and Naropa University.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Alex Wayman (attested 1978).
George Saintsbury studied at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He taught Paul Demiéville and held a post at the University of Edinburgh from around 1895 to 1915.

George Santayana studied at Harvard (PhD ~1886–1890 under William James), Berlin, and Cambridge. He worked in philosophy and was a member of the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist who earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He directed Queen's College, Benares (~1879–1888), was Principal of Muir Central College (1888–1895) and Sanskrit College (~1899–1906), and was Registrar at Calcutta (~1907–1914).

George Turnour was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as a Supreme Council member (1818) and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue (1820).

George Uglow Pope, an Indologist and linguist, founded and headed Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870). He later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (~1884–1907).

George V. Bobrinskoy studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary (BA ~1923–1926) and Yale under Franklin Edgerton (~1926–1928). He spent his Indology and linguistics career teaching Sanskrit at the University of Chicago from 1927, retiring as Emeritus Professor (1951–1967).

George Watt studied at Aberdeen and Glasgow (M.B. and C.M. ~1871–1873). He was Professor of Botany at Presidency University (1873–1874), worked at the University of Calcutta (~1874–1879) and Indian Museum (~1894–1903), and lectured at Edinburgh (~1907–1910).
